references.text: Aaron shall be gathered to his fathers and shall not enter the land I have given the Israelites, because you were rebellious against my command at the waters of Meribah.
Moses and Aaron were disobedient to the Lord's command in the wilderness of Zin when the congregation quarreled, and they did not honor the Lord as holy before the eyes of the people at the water.
The Lord was also angry with Moses because of the people and said that he too should not enter the land.
Moses asks the Lord to let him see the good land, but the Lord refuses him permission to cross the Jordan because of the people.
Moses shall die on the mountain because he was unfaithful to the Lord at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh and did not honor him among the Israelites.
The Lord shows Moses the land but says that he shall not go over there. Moses dies in the land of Moab.
At the waters of Meribah they provoked the Lord's anger, and it went badly for Moses because of them, for they were rebellious against his Spirit.
The Lord, the God of hosts, him you shall keep holy. The theme of hallowing the Lord is connected to the failure of Moses and Aaron.
The author of Hebrews refers to those who did not enter into rest because of unbelief, which reflects the lack of faith shown by Moses and Aaron.
